articles.title: TrusTerra is building a battery health score to make used electric vehicles resellable
articles.text:
TrusTerra is building a battery health score to make used electric vehicles resellable
TrusTerra runs an online marketplace for pre-owned electric vehicles built around its own battery health rating, with instant-sale and dealer auction services alongside it.
India has been buying electric two-wheelers and cars in rising numbers, but the market for reselling them has not developed at the same pace. A used petrol vehicle can be priced on mileage and service history. A used electric one comes down to the state of its battery. The battery is the most expensive part of the vehicle, and a buyer cannot check it by simply looking.
was set up in 2024 to supply that missing piece of information. It was founded by Tanvir Singh, Saurabh Arora, Madhu Reddy and Chanakya Agarwal, who spent close to a year building quietly before announcing itself in August 2025. Singh, the CEO, was earlier a co-founder at the battery-swapping venture Mooving. The founding team's background covers mobility, financial technology and battery systems.
The company says resale penetration in India's electric vehicle market remains under 2%. By that measure, sellers are exposed to steep depreciation, buyers are uncertain about what they are paying for, and dealers have little reason to stock the category. Lenders and insurers face the same gap. Neither can price a battery that nobody has measured.
A score for the battery
The core product is TruEV Score, a rating that assesses a vehicle's battery health, range consistency and remaining useful life. TrusTerra describes it as the equivalent of a credit score for an electric vehicle: a single reference number that a buyer, a dealer, a financier and an insurer can each price against.
The platform pulls together vehicle data, battery diagnostics and analytics to produce a valuation. Two services sit on top of the score. TerraCash gives an owner a diagnostic and a bid, with payment offered within 24 hours. TerraBid is an auction marketplace for certified dealers, with financing, warranties and buyback options attached to listings.
The company says it has been running TruEV Score with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and fleet operators to test it against their own valuation and lending decisions.
The plan for 20 cities
TrusTerra raised Rs 9 crore, about $1 million, in a pre-seed round announced in October 2025. The round was co-led by Finvolve and India Accelerator, with co-investment from GrowthCap Ventures.
Angel investors in the round included Shishir Maheswari of Eversource Capital, Samrath Jit Singh of Trontek Batteries, Ayush Lohia of Lohia Auto, and Kapil Nirmal, alongside other investors from the electric vehicle and financial technology sectors. TrusTerra's stated goal is for TruEV Score to be used across the industry as a common reference, rather than only on its own platform.
At the time of the round, the company said it had onboarded more than 150 dealers, evaluated over 2,000 used electric vehicles and facilitated transactions worth more than Rs 3 crore.
The funds are going into scaling the score, expanding the marketplace out of Delhi NCR into Bengaluru, Pune and Hyderabad along with smaller cities, and senior hiring across technology, operations and business development. Building partnerships with manufacturers, banks, non-banking lenders and dealer networks is part of the same plan.
TrusTerra has said it intends to certify 20,000 used electric vehicles across more than 20 cities within 18 months of the round. The marketplace runs on web and mobile, and lets customers, dealers and financiers trade vehicles with a verified battery score and financing attached.
(This story has been researched and compiled using publicly available information.)

articles.title: La nueva victoria de la Unión Europea: que te reparen un dispositivo incluso fuera de garantía entra en vigor el 31 de julio
articles.text:
Se dice mucho eso de que Europa inventa poco y regula mucho. Lo primero no es cierto y tenemos algunas de las empresas que dan vida a sectores como el de la IA y los semiconductores. Lo segundo sí, traduciéndose en la llegada del USB-C a los iPhone o las nuevas Nintendo Switch con una batería más fácil de reparar. Estos últimos años, Europa ha realizado avances para proteger al consumidor ante algo que gusta mucho a los fabricantes: la obsolescencia programada.
Y ahora, con la Directiva 2024/1799 a punto de entrar en juego, es interesante ver qué implica para nosotros como consumidores la que se ha bautizado como la directiva del derecho a reparar.
Directiva (UE) 2024/1799. Este es su nombre oficial y engloba un conjunto de normas comunes para promover la reparación de bienes. Se formalizó el 10 de junio de 2024 y modifica reglamentos y directivas de la Unión Europea previamente establecidos con el objetivo de alargar la vida útil de los productos, evitar la sustitución prematura y hacer que la reparación sea más accesible y atractiva para los consumidores.
En esencia, busca que se generen menos residuos o basura electrónica, así como favorecer la economía circular, pero evidentemente también busca promover que un usuario tenga más fácil reparar una lavadora, por ejemplo, antes que optar por comprar una nueva tirando la vieja en el punto limpio. De hecho, se fija que, siempre que el dispositivo sea reparable y el coste sea proporcionado, se pueda reparar fuera del periodo de garantía legal.
Calendario. La Directiva entró formalmente en vigor en junio de 2024, pero como siempre en estos casos, los diferentes países tenían un margen de tiempo para adaptarla a las normas internas. Ese tiempo está llegando a su fin, ya que este 31 de junio acaba el plazo para que los estados hayan preparado sus propuestas.
De cara al 31 de julio de 2027 se tendrá que dar un paso más para construir una plataforma europea online que permita a los consumidores encontrar fácilmente reparadores y vendedores de dispositivos restaurados. El fin es acabar con 35 millones de toneladas de residuos anuales en Europa, pero... ¿y la práctica?
"Derecho a reparar". Con esto en mente, los fabricantes deberán proporcionar acceso a piezas de recambio, información sobre la reparación y el mantenimiento, así como las herramientas de software necesarias para ejecutar esa reparación. La clave está en que los precios deben ser "razonables" para que no disuadan al consumidor para que no repare el dispositivo y, además, todo esto debe mantenerse durante los periodos de garantía fijados por los países. En el caso de España, tres años.
No termina ahí la cosa. Si el usuario quiere reparar el dispositivo, los fabricantes están obligados a prestar bienes de sustitución mientras dure esa reparación o a ofrecer bienes reacondicionados cuando la reparación sea imposible. Que si no se puede reparar por un defecto de fábrica y no por mal uso, no te quedes sin 'cacharro' o te toque comprar uno nuevo, en definitiva.
Para ello, la Directiva crea un 'Formulario' que los reparadores deben facilitar de forma gratuita al consumidor para informar sobre todo esto de la forma más clara y comprensible posible. Ahí se estipula el tipo de reparación, el precio, el plazo, las garantías sobre la reparación y cualquier otro término necesario, todo esto vigente durante 30 días naturales para que el usuario tome la decisión. Además, en caso de que se quiera reparar el dispositivo, la garantía se amplía un año adicional. Y esto es algo que puede hacer el fabricante directamente o mediante la subcontratación del servicio.
Impacto. Como decimos, los diferentes países de la Unión se han tenido que preparar este último año para un nuevo marco con el que esperan conseguir que la reparación sea más sencilla o que los fabricantes hagan productos que duren más tiempo. Hay algunos que son irreparables, pero en la práctica, el impacto de esta medida llega para fijar requisitos de reparabilidad en dispositivos como electrodomésticos, algunos equipos electrónicos como smartphones, consolas, ordenadores y ese tipo de bienes.
En caso de que algo falle en el dispositivo y no sea por un mal uso, puedes hacer valer tus derechos como consumidor. Pero claro, los fabricantes no estarán contentos dando todas las facilidades, y aquí es donde entra la importancia de conocer esos derechos.
Mi compañero Pepu ya plasmó eso en Xataka Móvil, una serie de recomendaciones que son de lo más útiles de cara a tener algo más de tranquilidad de cara al futuro de nuestros dispositivos:
- Plazos y documentación: en España, cualquier teléfono móvil nuevo y otros dispositivos cuentan por ley con tres años de garantía. Pide siempre el comprobante o factura de compra, guárdalo en formato digital y físico, y no lo pierdas, pues es imprescindible para gestionar cualquier reclamación.
- Sobre quién recae la responsabilidad: durante los dos primeros años, si el servicio técnico rechaza reparar tu dispositivo argumentando que lo has usado mal, no te conformes con una simple revisión a primera vista. Exige siempre que certifiquen y demuestren dicho mal uso mediante un informe detallado y por escrito.
- Accesorios: elementos como el cable, el cargador o los auriculares que vienen dentro de la caja no tienen una cobertura menor de un año por ser consumibles. La normativa les concede exactamente los mismos tres años de garantía que al propio teléfono.
- Prórroga de garantía: si tu dispositivo se avería dentro del periodo de garantía, tramitar su reparación te permitirá obtener un año más de protección legal añadida, de acuerdo con las directivas europeas.
- Registra todo: si se niegan a atenderte o intentan despacharte rápido en el servicio técnico, no te rindas. Eleva tu caso comunicándote con el servicio oficial de atención al cliente del fabricante (ya sea por teléfono o por internet) mencionando la ley correspondiente. Si nada de eso funciona, pides la hoja de reclamaciones para acudir a las autoridades de Consumo.

articles.title: Ace Combat 8 requires ray tracing GPU, 32GB RAM, and 125GB storage for recommended settings
articles.text:
TL;DR: Bandai Namco has revealed the official system requirements for playing Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve on PC, surprising fans with its unexpectedly steep hardware demands. Scheduled for release on October 2 for PS5, Xbox Series, and PC, it is the eighth mainline installment in the franchise and the sequel to 2019's Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown.
The minimum processor requirement for playing Ace Combat 8 at low settings is relatively modest, but gamers will still need an SSD with at least 125GB of free space, a graphics card that supports hardware-accelerated ray tracing, and DirectX 12 with Shader Model 6.6 or higher. The game also requires Windows 11, meaning PCs still running Windows 10 will have to be upgraded to run it.
Minimum System Requirements (1080p Upscaled / 30FPS, low settings)
- Processor: Intel Core i7-10700K / AMD Ryzen 5 3600X
- Memory: 16GB RAM
- Graphics: Nvidia RTX 2060 (6GB) or AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT (8GB)
Recommended System Requirements (1080p Upscaled / 60fps, medium settings)
- Processor: Intel Core i7-12700K or AMD Ryzen 5 5600X
- Memory: 32GB RAM
- Graphics: Nvidia RTX 3070 (8GB) or AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT (16GB)
Bandai Namco did not announce the requirements to play the game at max settings and at higher resolutions.
Built using Unreal Engine 5, Ace Combat 8 will feature fast-paced, arcade-style flight gameplay with hyper-realistic visuals and thrilling combat action, including high-octane aerial dogfights against enemy pilots and former allies. It will also feature massive land battleship boss fights, including Land Battleship No. 1, Xanthos, during Campaign Mission 9, "The Land Battleship Blockade."
The Steam listing for Ace Combat 8 confirms that the game will use Denuvo Anti-Tamper as third-party DRM, despite concerns about activation restrictions and the additional strain it could place on hardware resources. The store page also notes that the game will use kernel-level Easy Anti-Cheat for its multiplayer modes and limit players to five activations per day.
Ace Combat 8 is set in July 2029, when the Federation of Central Usea is invaded by the neighboring Republic of Sotoa. Players assume the role of a combat pilot and lead an uprising against the occupying forces. Despite lacking the resources to match the invaders, the surviving members of the FCU military fight back against the Sotoan occupation in an effort to reclaim their homeland.

articles.title: beyerdynamic Introduces the New DT 275 PRO Headphones
articles.text:
Tuesday, July 28th 2026
	
	
	
	beyerdynamic Introduces the New DT 275 PRO Headphones
German audio specialist beyerdynamic is expanding its popular PRO series with the new DT 275 PRO headphones. Designed for professional users, they enable quick and reliable sound assessments even in noisy environments. The new on-ear headphones combine high passive sound isolation with a design that makes them a portable and versatile companion. The DT 275 PRO is available now at a price of €119.00.
Raising the bar for passive sound isolation
Audio professionals often need to evaluate audio tracks quickly and in challenging acoustic environments. For example, while monitoring sound on set, working in mobile editing workflows, or carrying out a quick signal check at the mixing desk. Background noise can obscure important audio details, which can affect the quality of production and mixing decisions.The DT 275 PRO from beyerdynamic is a new monitoring headphone designed specifically to meet these requirements. Thanks to its industry-leading passive noise isolation, the DT 275 PRO enables a reliable assessment of audio signals, even in noisy working environments. FOH engineers, content creators, camera crews and DJs can therefore focus on what matters most: making informed decisions based on clearly audible audio signals, regardless of external distractions.
Designed for intensive production days
Mobile productions place high demands not only on monitoring, but also on comfort and flexibility. This is why the DT 275 PRO has been designed as a compact on-ear model. Weighing less than 200 grams, it remains comfortable to wear even during long sessions. For transport, the ear cups can be swiveled inwards to save space, allowing the headphones to be easily stowed away in production and equipment bags.
The cable connection on both sides offers additional flexibility. The connection cable can be attached to either the left or right ear cup and securely locked in place. This keeps it safely connected even during rapid movements in live or production settings. At the same time, the cable route can be adapted to the specific workflow, ensuring that the cable does not run unnecessarily through the workspace. This reduces potential sources of interference and ensures consistently reliable monitoring throughout the entire production process.
No need for compromises with the DT 275 PRO
The new on-ear headphones are made from robust materials, making them ideal for everyday use in demanding professional settings where audio equipment undergoes heavy use. High-quality faux leather ear pads and a soft, flexible headband provide a high level of comfort, even during prolonged use. All cushion components can be easily replaced and reordered. This allows production teams to comply with hygiene regulations and significantly extend the headphones' lifespan.
The DT 275 PRO will be available from July 28, 2026, at a recommended retail price of €119.00 (including VAT) in the online shop at www.beyerdynamic.de and from authorized retailers. Replaceable components and spare parts can be reordered separately.

articles.title: Panneaux solaires sur les rails : pourquoi la fausse bonne idée de la SNCF se heurte à la réalité — Frandroid
articles.text:
Un peu plus de 143 centimètres séparent les deux rails d’une voie ferrée. Un espace suffisant, selon certaines entreprises, pour y intégrer des panneaux photovoltaïques et transformer les infrastructures ferroviaires en sources de production d’électricité.
En France, la SNCF s’intéresse également à cette possibilité. Avec plus de 40 000 kilomètres de voies ferrées exploitées, le groupe ferroviaire étudie la manière dont ses infrastructures pourraient contribuer à diversifier son mix énergétique. Plusieurs projets pilotes sont actuellement en cours, certains ayant été lancés dès l’année dernière.
Des panneaux solaires amovibles testés sur les infrastructures ferroviaires
L’entreprise énergétique Bankset figure parmi les principaux partenaires de la SNCF dans le développement de cette technologie. La société a mis au point des panneaux solaires conçus pour être montés en moins de deux minutes sur les rails.
L’année dernière, selon Révolution Énergétique, un premier projet pilote baptisé « La Grosse Bankset Beta 1 » a été déployé sur un site technique parisien du groupe ferroviaire. Cette centrale solaire expérimentale fait depuis l’objet d’un suivi. Depuis le début de l’année 2026, une deuxième version du dispositif est également installée pour poursuivre les essais.
Pour rappel, la SNCF collabore également avec l’entreprise suisse Sun-Ways, qui développe aussi des solutions de centrales solaires ferroviaires. En avril 2025, un projet pilote d’une centaine de mètres a ainsi été lancé à Buttes, dans le canton de Neuchâtel, en Suisse.
Ces tests doivent permettre de recueillir des données essentielles sur la faisabilité technique du dispositif, sa production électrique réelle ainsi que la résistance des panneaux face aux contraintes propres au milieu ferroviaire.
Le groupe français étudie également l’installation de panneaux photovoltaïques sur des voies non circulées. De janvier à juin 2025, un prototype de centrale solaire (le système Solveig, développé par l’agence AREP) a été testé dans les Yvelines, au technicentre d’Achères de la SNCF. À l’issue de cette expérimentation, un déploiement plus large, notamment sur certaines lignes inutilisées à travers la France, a été envisagé.
Une technologie prometteuse mais encore limitée
Même si les rails photovoltaïques représentent une piste intéressante pour produire de l’électricité, la technologie reste encore au stade expérimental. Avant d’envisager un déploiement à grande échelle, plusieurs paramètres doivent encore être validés (résistance des panneaux aux vibrations, leur durée de vie, leur rendement réel, les coûts d’installation et de maintenance).
Même en cas de généralisation, la technologie ne devrait représenter qu’une contribution limitée face aux besoins énergétiques de la SNCF. Premier consommateur d’électricité en France, le groupe utilise près de 9 TWh d’électricité chaque année.
À titre de comparaison, la production annoncée par Bankset pour un kilomètre équipé correspondrait à la consommation d’environ une centaine de foyers. Il faudrait donc théoriquement plusieurs centaines de kilomètres d’installations pour alimenter l’équivalent de 40 000 foyers, ce qui reste très inférieur aux besoins du groupe ferroviaire.
D’ailleurs, en matière de solaire, le groupe mise davantage sur des solutions photovoltaïques plus classiques. Avec sa filiale SNCF Renouvelables créée en 2023, l’entreprise prévoit notamment d’installer des panneaux solaires sur ses propriétés : toitures de gares, parkings, bâtiments techniques, et foncier. Ces surfaces offrent un potentiel plus important et plus facilement exploitable.

articles.title: SA VC exits show early signs of a maturing venture capital ecosystem - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South Africa’s venture capital ecosystem is beginning to close one of the most important gaps in its growth story, according to two new studies. Exits.
Two new studies by the SA SME Fund, Endeavor South Africa and SAVCA claim to provide “compelling evidence” that local venture capital can deliver both meaningful investor returns and broader economic impact. Together, they show that South African venture-backed scale-ups are generating successful exits, while the asset class itself is producing realised returns broadly consistent with more mature international venture capital markets.
The broader South African Venture Capital: Exit & Performance Analysis, which looked at 226 realised exits reported by South African venture capital fund managers between 2009 and 2026, found that realised cash returns substantially exceeded invested capital, with capital-weighted realised returns ranging from 2.01x to 2.45x invested capital across the scenarios analysed.
The research also found that South African venture capital has delivered realised return characteristics broadly in line with those observed in more mature markets, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe and India, providing growing evidence that venture capital is becoming an increasingly attractive asset class for long-term investors.
The Exit Case Studies Analysis, meanwhile, looks at 18 South African venture capital-backed exits across 21 investment rounds between 2014 and 2026. It found that the sampled exits delivered a median gross internal rate of return (IRR) of 54 per cent, a median gross money-on-invested-capital (MOIC) of 3.5x, and a median valuation at exit of approximately ZAR1.6 billion (US$97.5 million).
Beyond investor returns, the broader high-growth sector that these companies operate in, has seen revenue growth by 256 per cent and employment growing by 49 per cent since 2021. Collectively, the exited companies created more than 4,000 direct jobs, averaging around 230 South African jobs per company, highlighting the broader economic impact of South Africa’s high-growth scale-ups.
Together, the findings suggest South Africa’s venture capital ecosystem is moving beyond isolated success stories towards a more mature investment market capable of attracting greater institutional capital.
While the market remains relatively young by global standards, the data points to a clear shift – exits are increasing in size, pathways are diversifying, and several landmark transactions have taken place in the past two years. Recent examples include Mastercard’s pending acquisition of BVNK, RapidDeploy’s acquisition by Motorola Solutions, iKhokha’s acquisition by Nedbank, Adumo’s acquisition by Lesaka, Quicket’s acquisition by Ticketmaster, and Optasia’s listing on the JSE.
Ketso Gordhan, CEO of the SA SME Fund, says the emergence of stronger exit evidence is significant because exits are the mechanism through which venture capital proves its ability to recycle capital, reward risk and attract new investment into the ecosystem.
“South Africa has long had entrepreneurial talent, credible founders and strong technology capability. What has been less visible is the proof that investors can realise meaningful returns from backing these companies. These studies show that the exit market is no longer theoretical. It is starting to happen, and it is happening across different pathways,” he said.
The report identifies four main exit routes now active in the South African venture capital ecosystem – international mergers and acquisitions, domestic mergers and acquisitions, secondary transactions and, more recently, IPOs. International M&A has historically been the most common route, with South African-built companies being acquired by global strategic buyers.
However, domestic M&A has gained traction, particularly in fintech, as banks, insurers, retailers and listed technology businesses increasingly acquire or partner with scale-ups to strengthen their own digital capabilities. Secondaries are emerging as an increasingly important liquidity route as larger scale-ups attract international growth capital.
Alison Collier, managing director of Endeavor South Africa, said the data shows that South African scale-ups are no longer only building for local relevance.
“The strongest companies in this study were built from South Africa, but not only for South Africa. They solved real market problems, used technology to scale efficiently, and in many cases expanded into regional or global markets. It is this combination that makes them attractive to acquirers and investors,” she said.
“The missing piece in the South African venture story has been exits. We are now seeing evidence that this gap is closing. This is critical because exits create confidence. They return capital to investors, reward founders and employees, and create the next generation of investors, mentors and repeat entrepreneurs.”
SAVCA CEO Anusha Naidu said the combined findings provided important evidence for institutional investors assessing South African venture capital as an asset class.
“The ability to demonstrate realised exits is fundamental to the development of any private capital market,” she said.
“These studies show that South African venture-backed companies are beginning to deliver realised return characteristics comparable with more mature international markets, while also contributing to employment, innovation and financial inclusion. This provides important evidence for pension funds, family offices, development finance institutions and other long-term capital providers evaluating venture capital as part of a diversified investment portfolio.”

articles.title: Incendie en France : Starlink est prêt à activer son service satellite d'urgence
articles.text:
Les feux de forêt continuent de ravager la Gironde, avec 42 000 hectares brûlés. Alors que l’incendie s’est progressivement stabilisé, malgré quelques reprises maîtrisées près de Lacanau et du Cap Ferret, Starlink a offert son aide aux Français sinistrés.
La filiale de SpaceX se dit prête à « aider les familles, les communautés et les entreprises disposant de smartphones LTE compatibles à rester connectées par SMS là où les réseaux terrestres sont indisponibles ». Concrètement, Starlink est en mesure de déployer gratuitement son service de connectivité d’urgence en France. Il permettra aux personnes sur place, que ce soit les victimes ou les entreprises, de se connecter au réseau mobile pour échanger des SMS.
When emergencies happen, speed counts. Starlink’s teams move fast to enable free connectivity when and where it’s needed most.
Starlink Mobile stands ready to also activate service in France—if granted regulatory approval—to help families, communities and businesses with… https://t.co/71T0O9cPVC
— Starlink (@Starlink) July 27, 2026
Baptisé Direct-to-Cell, le dispositif proposé par Starlink permet aux téléphones compatibles de se connecter automatiquement au réseau satellitaire dès que le réseau terrestre classique devient indisponible, sans manipulation particulière de la part de l’utilisateur. C’est une véritable béquille en cas de défaillances durables du réseau mobile des opérateurs. Le service reste toutefois limité à l’envoi de SMS. Il n’est pas possible de passer des appels.
À lire aussi : Elon Musk menace de couper Starlink au-dessus de l’Europe – l’histoire d’un bras de fer fou
Une offre qui n’a pas encore été acceptée
La société d’Elon Musk précise que sa proposition n’a pas encore été approuvée par les autorités françaises. Le service de connectivité d’urgence ne pourra être activé que « sous réserve d’obtenir l’autorisation des autorités réglementaires » en France. Pour le moment, les autorités n’ont pas encore réagi à la proposition du groupe américain.
« En cas d’urgence, la rapidité est essentielle. Les équipes de Starlink interviennent vite pour assurer une connectivité gratuite là où et quand elle est le plus nécessaire », déclare Starlink.
Avant de proposer son aide à la France, Starlink a d’abord activé son service gratuitement en Espagne, pour les clients MásOrange et Movistar touchés par les incendies près de Madrid.
Starlink Mobile is providing free connectivity to @MASORANGE_ES and @movistar_es customers in regions affected by the wildfires near Madrid.
Families, communities and businesses with compatible LTE smartphones can now stay connected through SMS even if terrestrial networks are…
— Starlink (@Starlink) July 26, 2026
Face à la crise en Gironde, Orange et Bouygues Telecom ont de leur côté annoncé offrir 200 Go de données supplémentaires, ainsi que des appels et SMS illimités, aux abonnés résidant dans les zones sinistrées, et ce, jusqu’au 31 août 2026.

articles.title: Fini WhatsApp : la France choisit sa propre messagerie et veut convertir l'Europe
articles.text:
Tchap, la messagerie instantanée exclusivement réservée aux agents publics de l’État français, a été lancée en avril 2018. Sept ans plus tard, soit en juillet 2025, François Bayrou signait une circulaire imposant l’adoption de la plateforme comme messagerie sécurisée de référence de l’État. En octobre 2025, une nouvelle étape, et non des moindres, a été franchie : la Direction interministérielle du numérique (DINUM) a rejoint la Fondation Matrix, soit l’organisme chargé de superviser le développement du protocole open source et décentralisé Matrix, sur lequel repose Tchap.
La France est ainsi devenue le premier État à siéger dans sa gouvernance. Dès lors, la DINUM a pu participer à la gouvernance de la Fondation Matrix et contribuer à l’évolution du protocole Matrix, avant que d’autres pays, comme l’Allemagne, la Suède et le Luxembourg, ne la rejoignent quelque temps plus tard.
Une souveraineté numérique nationale, mais aussi bientôt européenne grâce au protocole Matrix ?
Avec Tchap, l’objectif de l’État français est de proposer une messagerie instantanée, chiffrée de bout en bout et hébergée sur le cloud du ministère de l’Intérieur, afin de consolider son autonomie numérique. Exit la messagerie américaine WhatsApp et la plateforme Telegram d’origine russe, jugées inadaptées aux exigences de souveraineté numérique, et place au protocole britannique Matrix.
Mais la France ne vise plus seulement une souveraineté numérique nationale : l’objectif est maintenant une adoption européenne de Matrix afin de « consolider un écosystème numérique européen sécurisé et interopérable ». La Bundeswehr allemande, l’administration suédoise et le gouvernement luxembourgeois ont déjà adopté le protocole Matrix ; la France veut maintenant inciter d’autres pays à suivre le mouvement, notamment en organisant des événements destinés à « promouvoir l’utilisation de Matrix et défendre les valeurs de l’open source ».
La DINUM et la Fondation Matrix travaillent sur deux chantiers majeurs, tout en anticipant les « défis futurs »
Dans un bilan faisant état de sa collaboration avec la Fondation Matrix, la DINUM explique travailler principalement sur « deux chantiers majeurs ». Le premier, la recherche fédérée d’utilisateurs (MSC Federated User Search), vise à permettre à un agent de retrouver un contact hébergé sur un autre serveur Matrix, y compris lorsque celui-ci se trouve dans un autre pays. Le second, baptisé Simple Border Gateway (SBG), agit comme une passerelle sécurisée entre plusieurs organisations disposant chacune de leur propre instance Matrix. À terme, il pourrait permettre à un agent français utilisant Tchap de communiquer directement avec un agent allemand ou luxembourgeois depuis une autre instance Matrix, sans dépendre d’une messagerie commerciale privée.
Cela n’est pas tout, puisque la DINUM annonce aussi se préparer aux menaces liées à la cryptographie post-quantique. En effet, les ordinateurs quantiques pourraient être un jour capables de compromettre les algorithmes de chiffrement actuels, mettant ainsi potentiellement en péril des données sensibles de l’État. À terme, ces évolutions doivent permettre à Tchap de rester compatible avec les futurs standards de cybersécurité, tout en renforçant les échanges sécurisés entre administrations européennes.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 28, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 28, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, July 28, 2026.
From Instamart naming ex-Myntra chief Nandita Sinha as CEO to Inflexor Ventures securing Rs 400 Cr for Fund III, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest news
Instamart names former Myntra chief Nandita Sinha as CEO
Instamart has appointed former Myntra chief executive officer Nandita Sinha as its new CEO, handing leadership of one of India’s largest quick-commerce businesses to a seasoned consumer internet executive at a time when the sector is entering a more competitive and profitability-focused phase.
Sinha will take charge on August 3, 2026, succeeding Amitesh Jha, who led the business through a period of rapid expansion.
Inflexor Ventures raises Rs 400 Cr as first close of Fund III
Early-stage, sector-agnostic venture capital firm Inflexor Ventures has announced the first close of its third fund, securing commitments of Rs 400 crore towards its target corpus of Rs 1,250 crore.
The fund, named the Inflexor Technology Discovery Fund, is backed by anchor investors including the Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund, HDFC Asset Management Company (HDFC AMC), and HDFC AMC Select AIF FoF (HDFC FoF). It has also attracted commitments from several leading international institutional investors, the firm said in a statement.
Funding news
House of Student raises $2M in seed funding
House of Student, a student accommodation marketplace, has raised $2 million in a seed funding round comprising equity and debt. The round was led by Saltwater Sutra and Nirmitsu Inspirational Ventures, with participation from strategic investors and existing backers of Unilodgers.
The funding will be used to expand the company's global presence, enhance its AI capabilities, grow its accommodation supply and develop new products. Founded by Vaibhav Verma, House of Student operates a marketplace with more than 2.5 million verified student rooms across over 25 countries.
Hegdinvst raises $1.3M in Series A funding
Hegdinvst, a Chennai-based alternative investment manager, has raised $1.3 million (Rs 11.5 crore) in an oversubscribed Series A funding round backed by domestic and international high-net-worth investors. The capital will primarily fund the sponsor and manager commitment for the firm's proposed SEBI Category III Alternative Investment Fund, a multi-asset hedge fund.
Founded by Aditya Bhandari, Hegdinvst manages investment strategies across private and public markets through its alternative investment funds, serving family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals and other investors.
Yaanendriya raises Rs 15 Cr from Piper Serica
Yaanendriya, a Bengaluru-based deeptech company developing sensor, navigation and control technologies for autonomous systems, has raised Rs 15 crore in funding from venture capital firm Piper Serica. The investment will be used to strengthen research and development, accelerate product development and expand the company's portfolio of high-precision navigation systems.
Yaanendriya develops technologies for drones, ground robots, spacecraft and underwater vehicles, with products designed to operate in GNSS-denied environments. The company also plans to advance indigenous MEMS accelerometer and gyroscope technologies for aerospace and autonomous applications.
Other news
Invest Qatar opens India office to boost investment ties
Invest Qatar has opened a dedicated office in India as part of efforts to strengthen investment ties between the two countries and support Indian companies expanding into Qatar. During a visit to New Delhi and Mumbai, representatives met businesses, investors and startups to discuss opportunities across the Gulf and Middle East.
The new office, led by Tanaz Buhariwalla, will assist companies with market entry, regulatory processes and business expansion. Invest Qatar said the move builds on growing economic cooperation and aims to encourage more Indian businesses to establish operations in Qatar.
Nielsen launches AI-powered advertising intelligence platform
Nielsen has launched Ad Intel AI, an AI-powered platform that provides real-time advertising intelligence across media channels. The platform combines Nielsen's advertising data with AI to help users analyse competitor spending, creative strategies and market trends, while supporting decision-making across planning and campaign analysis.
Ad Intel AI covers 5.5 million brands and 4.6 million advertisers across 23 media types in more than 90 markets. The launch marks the first in a series of AI-powered products Nielsen plans to introduce as it expands its media intelligence and advertising measurement offerings.
SNITCH acquires womenswear brand Berrylush
SNITCH has acquired womenswear brand Berrylush, marking its entry into the women's fashion market and expanding beyond menswear. Berrylush will continue to operate under its existing brand while using SNITCH's capabilities in product development, technology, supply chain, marketing and omnichannel retail.
The companies will work together to accelerate product innovation, expand retail presence and strengthen the customer experience. The acquisition supports SNITCH's strategy of building a portfolio of fashion brands and increasing its presence in India's growing apparel market.
PureSil launches mineral paint with silicification technology
PureSil Paints has launched PureSil Interior-Exterior Mineral Paint, introducing its silicification technology to the Indian decorative paints market. The zero-VOC mineral coating is made using silicate binders derived from rice husk ash and fly ash, and is designed to bond chemically with masonry rather than form a surface film.
The company said the paint offers improved moisture regulation, UV resistance, fire protection and mould resistance, while reducing reliance on petroleum-based materials. PureSil is initially available through authorised dealers in Nagpur, Vadodara, Raipur and Kolkata at an introductory price of Rs 320 per litre.
BlackLine launches AI tool for financial reconciliations
BlackLine has launched Verity Prepare, an AI-powered platform designed to automate account reconciliation and other financial close processes. The system uses multiple AI agents to analyse supporting documents, match transactions, identify discrepancies and prepare audit-ready reconciliations, while allowing finance teams to review and approve the results.
BlackLine said early adopters reduced manual reconciliation preparation time by up to 92%. The launch expands the company's AI offerings for finance teams, with a focus on improving efficiency while maintaining governance, transparency and human oversight.
GoKwik and PayU launch AI shopping experience on ChatGPT
GoKwik and PayU have launched an AI-powered shopping experience on ChatGPT that enables consumers to discover, compare and buy products from multiple Indian direct-to-consumer brands within a single conversation. The platform is live with brands including Hyphen, Beardo and Kilrr, with more merchants expected to join through the GoKwik ecosystem.
Consumers can complete purchases using PayU's payment infrastructure, supporting UPI, cards, net banking and wallets. The companies said the platform allows D2C brands to offer AI-enabled shopping without requiring additional integration or engineering work.
Studio Blo launches AI advertising division
Studio Blo has launched a premium AI-native advertising division, bringing together a team of filmmakers and creative professionals to produce AI-powered branded content and advertising campaigns. The new division includes filmmakers and specialists from India and overseas, spanning automotive, food, advertising and cinematography.
Studio Blo said the unit will combine AI technologies, including celebrity cloning and performance capture, with traditional filmmaking to create commercial content. The launch expands the company's AI-driven production business, which has worked on advertising, entertainment and sports projects for brands and agencies in India and internationally.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: "El idioma alemán rompió nuestro juego": cómo una simple coma bastó para poner contra las cuerdas a un juego de Steam
articles.text:
La corrección de errores es una de las tareas más frustrantes en el desarrollo de videojuegos, especialmente cuando un fallo parece ocurrir de forma totalmente aleatoria y sin seguir ningún patrón. El mundo de los bugs en los videojuegos es muy curioso, y sino que se lo digan a los chicos de Atari, que al intentar centrar el logo de la empresa en el juego 'Tempest' acabaron implementando un fallo que permitía conseguir partidas infinitas.
Pues algo en esa línea le ha pasado a Black Beach Studios, desarrolladora de Iron Rebellion, un shooter de mechas para realidad virtual. En el estudio estuvieron meses enfrentándose a un enigma: los jugadores no dejaban de quejarse en Steam y en la tienda de Meta Quest de cierres inesperados en el juego. El problema era que en los reportes automáticos de fallos no aparecía absolutamente nada.
No fue hasta que el equipo empezó a recrear situaciones de juego muy específicas cuando dieron con una cadena de errores tan absurda que, viéndolo con perspectiva, casi parece una broma a pesar de tener todo el sentido del mundo.
Dos alemanes, una pelea y una caída hacia la izquierda
Según explican los propios desarrolladores en un vídeo publicado en TikTok, el origen del problema residía en una combinación de eventos extremadamente específica. El juego se colgaba exactamente cuando ocurría lo siguiente:
- Un mecha era destruido.
- Los restos del mecha caían hacia la izquierda.
- El combate tenía lugar en un punto muy concreto de un mapa específico.
- Y siempre había exactamente dos jugadores alemanes participando en la partida.
Ante esto, el equipo se hizo la pregunta lógica: ¿cómo es posible que el idioma de los jugadores haga que el juego se rompa? Los que sepáis de informática ya estaréis intuyendo la razón: los decimales, que los carga el diablo.
En informática, los números decimales son un asunto delicado. Mientras que en el mundo angloparlante se utiliza el punto como separador decimal (por ejemplo, 1.99), en países como Alemania se utiliza por defecto la coma (como hacemos en España, por ejemplo, con el 1,99). Si esto no se tiene en cuenta, los ingredientes para el desastre están servidos: debido a la localización al alemán, el juego, por alguna razón, convertía los puntos decimales en comas al calcular las posiciones físicas.
Cuando el mecha caía hacia la izquierda en ese punto concreto, el juego enviaba los datos de posición en paquetes de red al resto de jugadores. Debido a la configuración regional, estos paquetes contenían comas en lugar de puntos, lo que provocaba que el código de red de los demás jugadores no supiese interpretar la información. Los datos no se podían procesar y el juego se cerraba por completo de forma instantánea.
El problema ya ha sido solucionado y el juego es totalmente funcional, pero no es la primera vez que sucede algo parecido. De hecho, pasó algo similar en juego muy querido: 'The Witcher 2'. El juego tenía un fallo en la gestión de memoria y codificación de fuentes con los textos en alemán, de manera que cada vez que intentaba procesar un carácter con Umlaut (ä, ö, ü) o la ß, se rompía. Además, ocurría en cualquier contexto: al reproducirse en subtítulos, en el inventario... La comunidad tuvo que salir al rescate con un mod no oficial.

articles.title: SpaceX publie des photos du plasma entourant le Starship lors de sa descente hypersonique
articles.text:
On pourrait croire de prime abord à un rendu 3D extrait d’un blockbuster ou d’un jeu vidéo d’anticipation. Pourtant, les quatre nouveaux clichés dévoilés par SpaceX le 28 juillet 2026 décrivent une scène parfaitement réelle, qui a eu lieu lors du vol 13 du Starship, dans la nuit du 24 au 25 juillet — vol qui a été globalement un succès pour l’entreprise.
Du plasma tout autour du Starship
Le choc principal face à ces photos vient avant tout du spectacle proposé à la redescente hypersonique de l’étage supérieur de la fusée géante — le Ship, flanqué du numéro 40, comme on peut le voir sur certaines captures. À plus de 27 000 km/h, l’engin apparaît enveloppé d’un halo flamboyant oscillant entre le jaune incandescent, le magenta et le violet.
Ce n’est pas de la science-fiction ou un petit délire sur Photoshop, mais la conséquence d’un phénomène physique. À cette vitesse vertigineuse, l’atmosphère n’a pas le temps de s’écarter et se retrouve violemment écrasée contre la structure. Cette compression instantanée de l’air fait grimper la température à plusieurs milliers de degrés.
L’intensité du contact est d’ailleurs telle que les molécules d’oxygène et d’azote qui peuplent l’atmosphère se font disloquer. Le gaz se transforme alors en plasma ionisé, le fameux quatrième état de la matière. Et ici, la palette de couleurs capturée par les caméras embarquées renseigne sur les zones qui encaissent le plus durement.
Le jaune-blanc étincelant marque les points de pression et de chaleur maximales sous le ventre et les ailerons, tandis que les teintes violacées traduisent la « détente » du gaz le long du fuselage. Ces couleurs étaient déjà visibles lors d’autres vols d’essai du Starship, par exemple durant les 5e et 10e tentatives.

articles.title: La guerre des géants : Amazon défie aussi Starlink sur le terrain du mobile, tout ce qu’il faut savoir
articles.text:
Amazon veut, elle aussi, connecter les smartphones à ses satellites. Le géant de l’e-commerce se lance officiellement dans la course du « direct-to-device », et risque bien de faire trembler Starlink.
Amazon Leo, la constellation qui vise à apporter une connexion Internet haut débit dans les zones reculées grâce à des antennes, compte déjà plus de 390 satellites en orbite et vise une mise en service dès cette année.
Mais avant même d’avoir stabilisé ce front, l’entreprise ouvre une seconde ligne d’attaque : le mobile. Elle vient de déposer une demande auprès de la Commission fédérale des communications (FCC) pour déployer plus de 5 000 satellites capables de se connecter directement aux téléphones des utilisateurs.
Un réseau mobile signé Amazon
Concrètement, ce futur réseau doit permettre d’appeler, d’envoyer des messages, de naviguer sur Internet ou encore de déclencher une alerte d’urgence, directement depuis un smartphone classique, même là où aucune antenne terrestre ne capte. Mais ce n’est pas tout, puisqu’Amazon vise aussi les objets connectés et la connectivité embarquée dans les véhicules.
Pour y parvenir, la société fondée par Jeff Bezos peut s’appuyer sur les fréquences acquises lors de son rachat de Globalstar en avril dernier, pour 11,6 milliards de dollars. Mais le chemin s’annonce semé d’embûches. Car Starlink domine allègrement ce marché naissant, avec des partenariats déjà opérationnels aux États-Unis via T-Mobile, et au Royaume-Uni avec Virgin Media O2.
La firme a également investi 20 milliards de dollars dans l’acquisition de fréquences auprès d’EchoStar afin de muscler son propre service mobile.
Qui l'emportera ?
À noter qu’Amazon doit également composer avec un handicap de taille : contrairement à SpaceX, le groupe ne dispose pas de son propre lanceur. Car la fusée New Glenn de Blue Origin reste clouée au sol depuis l’explosion de son pas de tir en mai. Un contretemps qui a déjà contraint Amazon à demander un délai à la FCC pour le déploiement de sa constellation Leo (et qui profite à une certaine Ariane 6).
Mais Amazon dispose malgré tout d’un atout de poids. Avec 255 milliards de dollars d’actifs, elle peut se permettre de prendre son temps, quand SpaceX doit composer avec des besoins en capitaux bien plus pressants. De même, la firme peut miser sur son infrastructure mondiale gigantesque pour soutenir ses nouvelles offres.
Reste, malgré tout, à voir si cette technologie trouvera preneur. Chez l’opérateur T-Mobile, le patron Srini Gopalan a révélé que l’usage satellite ne représentait que 0,0002 % du trafic total, concentré essentiellement autour des parcs nationaux.
Le direct-to-device consiste à connecter un smartphone standard directement à un satellite, sans antenne parabolique ni terminal dédié. Techniquement, le satellite joue le rôle d’une « tour cellulaire » très éloignée, avec des contraintes fortes sur la puissance d’émission du téléphone et la sensibilité des antennes côté satellite. À la différence d’un accès satellite classique (type modem/box satellite), le D2D vise surtout la couverture ponctuelle : messages, appels limités, alertes d’urgence, et un débit généralement inférieur à une connexion haut débit dédiée. La latence et la continuité de service dépendent aussi de la densité de la constellation et du passage des satellites au-dessus de l’utilisateur.
Les fréquences déterminent si un smartphone peut communiquer sans matériel spécial, car ses modems et antennes sont conçus pour des bandes cellulaires précises. Disposer de droits d’usage sur ces bandes (souvent via licences) permet d’émettre légalement et de limiter les interférences avec d’autres réseaux (cellulaires, GPS, autres satellites). Certaines bandes offrent de meilleures performances en couverture (meilleure pénétration, portée) au prix de moins de capacité, tandis que d’autres privilégient le débit mais exigent des conditions radio plus favorables. Sans fréquences adaptées et coordonnées au niveau réglementaire, un service D2D peut être bridé, géographiquement limité, ou bloqué par les autorités.
La FCC est l’autorité américaine qui attribue et encadre l’usage du spectre radio et autorise l’exploitation de systèmes satellitaires visant le marché américain. Elle impose des obligations techniques (risques d’interférences, partage du spectre, sécurité) et des jalons de déploiement : un opérateur doit mettre en orbite et rendre opérationnelle une partie de sa constellation dans des délais donnés. Une demande de délai sert à éviter la perte d’autorisations ou de priorités de fréquences si le calendrier industriel dérape. En pratique, ces décisions influencent la crédibilité du projet, la capacité à lever des fonds, et l’avantage concurrentiel face aux constellations déjà opérationnelles.

articles.title: Le cabriolet électrique que tout le monde attendait pourrait enfin exister, et c'est BMW qui s'y colle
articles.text:
Le constat est presque sans appel : en France, le nombre de cabriolets électriques neufs commercialisables se compte sur les doigts d’une seule main, avec notamment la Maserati GranCabrio Folgore et le MG Cyberster.
Et c’est à peu près tout si on met de côté la Fiat 500e cabriolet qui n’est pas du même calibre ou encore la Mini Cooper SE Cabriolet, produite à moins de 1 000 exemplaires en 2023.
Ailleurs, les projets s’accumulent surtout dans les tiroirs : Polestar a repoussé son roadster 6 sans nouvelle date, Tesla promet son Roadster depuis 2017 et vient encore de décaler sa présentation, et celui de Porsche semble encore incertain.
C’est dans ce contexte que BMW Blog annonce l’arrivée d’une BMW i4 Cabriolet, prévue pour 2028.
La Neue Klasse, un argument technique pour un cabriolet électrique
Sur le papier, l’architecture Neue Klasse, celle qui équipe déjà la berline i3, apporte une réponse crédible à un problème connu : un cabriolet électrique perd en rigidité structurelle ce qu’on lui retire en toit, et il faut compenser par du poids, l’ennemi numéro un de l’autonomie.
Avec une base annoncée à 700 km d’autonomie WLTP, et même jusqu’à 900 km pour la version la plus endurante, le tout avec une architecture 800 volts et une charge rapide en 400 kW, même une perte de 15 % liée au poids supplémentaire et à l’aérodynamique dégradée laisserait une autonomie confortable, autour de 600 km.
Le projet porterait le nom de code NA3, accompagné d’un coupé NA2 sur la même base comme le relate BMW Blog. Reste que la Série 4 Gran Coupé actuelle s’arrêterait l’an prochain, laissant l’appellation sans remplaçant pendant un an avant l’arrivée de ces 2 modèles dotés de 2 portes, si l’information se confirme.
Et la version thermique du cabriolet, elle, resterait produite jusqu’à mi-2029, avec environ un an de cohabitation entre les deux motorisations.
BMW fait de la résistance
BMW dispose d’un argument que peu de constructeurs peuvent avancer sur ce segment : une base de clients déjà installée et très fidèle à la gamme Série 4 Coupé et Série 4 Cabriolet. C’est d’ailleurs l’un des derniers constructeurs premium à proposer des cabriolets dans sa gamme, Mercedes et Audi les abandonnant peu à peu.
De quoi limiter le risque commercial par rapport à un roadster développé sur une plateforme dédiée. Mais 2028, c’est encore loin, et il peut encore se passer plein de choses dans l’univers de la voiture électrique, en particulier si les ventes de la BMW i3 ne décollent pas comme prévu. Mais pour le moment, à ce niveau, tout à l’air de bien se passer.

articles.title: You can now play Morrowind directly in your browser, no installation required
articles.text:
First look: A browser tab can now run Morrowind's engine, a game that once pushed desktop hardware to its limits. A new project called OpenMW-Web brings The Elder Scrolls III into a web browser using the OpenMW engine, rather than through streaming or emulation.
The project, shared by a developer known as /u/Dumpster_Buddy, is built on OpenMW, an open-source reimplementation of Morrowind's original engine. OpenMW was developed to support Windows, macOS, and Linux, and to reduce the bugs and limitations of the original 2002 engine.
The distinction is central to the project's technical appeal. Because it does not rely on streaming, the system avoids remote-server dependence. And since it does not use emulation, it keeps features such as shadows, water, saves, and gamepad support working.
The web app currently offers a self-contained "example world" that runs without any installation or external files, effectively acting as a test area for the engine in the browser. To access the full game, users must point the application to their own Morrowind data files. Once connected, the full game becomes playable, with options to change settings and save progress.
The developer said the system does not upload any files and currently works best on desktop versions of Chrome, Edge, and Brave. The setup relies on browser-based local file access.
While the browser version is functional, it is not positioned as a replacement for a traditional installation. Running OpenMW as a standalone application remains more straightforward. But the web-based approach shows how far browser technology has come in handling 3D graphics, input, and saved games.
The project also points to where enthusiast-driven development could go next. The developer has indicated plans to expand the feature set, including potential mod support and even multiplayer functionality. Those additions would make the project more capable, but it is just an experiment for now.
Recent efforts have also included a dual-screen implementation for handheld hardware. The browser version extends that experimentation into web-native territory.
There are still limitations. Early testing indicates that input handling, particularly mouse interaction in menus, can be inconsistent. These issues do not take away from the technical achievement. Running a game engine with rendering, physics, and input support inside a browser is a notable feat.
For now, OpenMW-Web remains an enthusiast project rather than a mainstream way to play. It requires user-supplied game data and some tolerance for rough edges. It also shows how open-source engines can give older games a new life in the browser.

articles.title: Act Security raises $60M to take action against agentic access sprawl at the infrastructure layer - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Act Security raises $60M to take action against agentic access sprawl at the infrastructure layer
Cloud security startup Act Security Ltd. says it’s primed and ready to help enterprises safely deploy artificial intelligence agents at large scale after raising $60 million in funding across two rounds.
The company was founded last year and closed on a hefty $20 million seed funding round led by Team8 and Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Caltech and Hetz Ventures. That round remained undisclosed until today, when it clinched yet more backing in the shape of a $40 million Series A investment led by Notable Capital, with participation from Startpoint Capital and SVCI.
Act Security says it’s launching its “action-centric” security platform in response to traditional cloud security models being stretched beyond their limits by the emergence of agentic AI systems. Traditionally, large organizations have slowly but surely enabled massive access across their cloud environments, but the vast majority of the permissions they’ve allowed are unneeded, essentially sitting dormant.
For instance, a contractor may once have been given access to a certain database system in order to fix something, and that access was never revoked, or an employee may have access to systems they never use. That has never really been much of an issue because of the slow speed at which human attackers operate.
But that’s no longer the case now that cyber attackers have access to extremely powerful AI tools. AI models and autonomous AI agents can operate at the speed of machines, and it’s a big concern. In the case of AI agents, many of them have inherited outdated human permissions, and it means that the misconfigurations and vulnerabilities that were once considered low priority because it would take so long to exploit them, can now be taken advantage of in seconds. Security teams that rely on traditional, reactive security patches are asking to be caught short.
This is why Act Security says its action-centric security platform is now so important. It’s designed to target risk at the infrastructure level, and rather than flooding security teams with alerts about misconfigurations, it tries to eliminate the permissions that make them exploitable in the first place.
This is done by systematically reducing the access surface across an organization’s cloud environments. It works by enforcing strict, deterministic boundaries that carefully control what human workers and AI agents can reach and what they can do when they get there. According to the startup’s co-founder and Chief Executive Jonathan Langer, it works by evaluating identities, networks and AI access simultaneously, enforcing the principle of least privilege access to ensure that agents can scale and do their work in the safest and most secure way.
Langer said something like 97% of cloud access permissions sit dormant and unused, which is fine for humans, but not so for AI agents. “They’re inheriting the same old human permissions, running around the clock at machine speed, with none of the judgment a person would apply,” he explained. “Visibility tools surface thousands of findings and leave teams triaging symptoms one by one, while the root cause, the access architecture, goes unaddressed. Instead of chasing findings, we remove the conditions that turn risk into a breach, making the cloud structurally secure before attacks unfold.”
With the launch of Act Security’s platform, organizations will be able to clean up their existing “access sprawl” and dramatically reduce their attack surface, while preventing their security from eroding over time. The startup’s platform continuously validates access boundaries and extends into the continuous integration and continuous deployment pipeline to block violations before application updates reach production.
When using Act Security, organizations will be able to deploy autonomous AI agents with greater confidence by tightly controlling what they can and can’t access. This will help to eliminate the exposed pathways that attackers use to move laterally across networks, Langer said. In other words, attackers will find that even if they break into something, they’ll find they have nowhere to go, limiting the impact of any security breach.
Team8 Managing Partner Liran Grinberg said Act Security noticed the extent of the access problem of AI agents before anyone else. “Cloud security has spent a decade telling organizations where their risk is,” he said. “Act is the first platform that actually removes it, and in an era where AI exploits exposure in minutes rather than months, that’s the new baseline.”

articles.text:
Tuesday, July 28th 2026
	
		
	
	
	Arctic Unveils the 10-port Arctic Fan Controller
The ARCTIC Fan Controller brings together intelligent fan management, detailed monitoring, and broad software compatibility in one compact solution. With support for up to ten independently controllable fans, it enables precise airflow optimization while simplifying the management of sophisticated cooling configurations. Extensive software compatibility, including open-source software and Linux support, ensures seamless integration into a wide range of systems.
The Fan Controller allows for true customization with independent channel control. Unlike daisy-chained hubs that share one signal, the ARCTIC Fan Controller lets you set unique speeds for every fan. Combined with open-source software, each fan can be monitored individually, making it easy to fine-tune cooling performance or to automate fan speeds based on workload. This results in improved system efficiency, enhanced reliability, and a more streamlined user experience.Engineered for Modern Systems
The Fan Controller is now available in the ARCTIC webshop - with a 25% discount. Also available, on Amazon, eBay, and from selected partners.

articles.title: Líder de tecnologia do Xbox chama falha de "inaceitável" e promete mudanças • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Líder de tecnologia do Xbox chama falha de “inaceitável” e promete mudanças
Scott Van Vliet classificou falha recente nos serviços do Xbox como uma situação inaceitável. O executivo prometeu melhorias para evitar novas quedas.
Scott Van Vliet classificou falha recente nos serviços do Xbox como uma situação inaceitável. O executivo prometeu melhorias para evitar novas quedas.
Uma instabilidade que dura alguns minutos ou algo em torno de uma hora é tolerável. Mas uma que dura quase um dia inteiro tira qualquer um do sério. Jogadores do Xbox passaram por isso na segunda-feira (27/07). O problema foi tão extenso que Scott Van Vliet, diretor de tecnologia da divisão Xbox, classificou o ocorrido como uma “situação inaceitável”.
A falha em questão afetou vários serviços do Xbox. Como consequência, muitos usuários tiveram dificuldade para fazer login em suas contas, acessar a sua biblioteca de jogos e até jogar alguns títulos já instalados em seus consoles. A pior parte é que o problema durou quase 20 horas.
É uma situação incomum. Instabilidades como essa até ocorrem, mas costumam ser solucionadas em pouco tempo. É por isso, provavelmente, que Vliet publicou um extenso texto no X para explicar o que aconteceu e prometer providências.
De acordo com o executivo, um serviço de licenciamento externo, mas do qual o ecossistema do Xbox depende, é que falhou. Além dos mencionados problemas que afetaram os jogadores, a instabilidade também prejudicou parceiros do Xbox que dependem do mesmo serviço.
Ainda de acordo com Vliet, o problema foi identificado ainda nas primeiras horas da segunda-feira por meio de um sistema automatizado de monitoramento. Uma equipe do Xbox redirecionou, então, o tráfego para as partes do sistema que ainda funcionavam enquanto a causa era buscada.
Essa abordagem fez o serviço voltar a funcionar de modo irregular em diferentes regiões, razão pela qual os usuários notaram o restabelecimento em momentos diferentes.
O próprio Vliet explicou, ainda que de um modo um tanto vago:
Estamos realizando uma análise completa pós-incidente. Me importo menos com a causa raiz resumida em uma única frase e mais com questões reais: por que uma falha em um serviço foi capaz de causar tanta instabilidade, por que a recuperação demorou tanto e o que mudaremos para que um único ponto de falha não arruíne sua noite novamente.
Isso significa fortalecer as dependências subjacentes ao login e à inicialização do jogo, aprimorar a forma como detectamos e controlamos esse tipo de falha e sermos mais rápidos e transparentes com você quando algo der errado.
Scott Van Vliet, diretor de tecnologia da divisão Xbox
A promessa feita pelo executivo pode envolver o tal sistema de licenciamento apontado como a origem do problema. Não ficou claro que sistema é esse. Mas, em resposta a um usuário no X, Vliet explicou que trata-se de um serviço da própria Microsoft que é compartilhado entre vários produtos da companhia.
O mesmo usuário respondeu, na sequência, que não gosta da ideia de que um serviço em outro lugar possa afetar o Xbox. Vliet respondeu então que os melhores sistemas contam com soluções resilientes para falhas em dependências e finalizou dizendo: “é aqui que vamos melhorar”.

articles.title: WhatsApp Web se actualiza y por fin puedes llamar sin abrir el móvil
articles.text:
WhatsApp ha añadido dos de las funciones más pedidas por los usuarios que utilizan la aplicación de mensajería en su ordenador. MEta anunció que la actualización más reciente de WhatsApp Web ahora ofrece llamadas de voz y vídeo sin necesidad de instalar nada adicional. Esta versión también debuta con otras mejoras pensadas para quienes alternan entre el móvil y el PC.
De acuerdo con el comunicado de prensa, desde hoy ya puedes hacer y recibir llamadas de audio y vídeo desde WhatsApp Web. La función está disponible tanto para llamadas individuales como grupales y cierra una brecha de varios años que mantenía a la aplicación web como un simple complemento para chatear. Si usas WhatsApp en Windows o macOS, el botón de las llamadas que se ubica en la parte superior de la conversación ya no te enviará a que descargues la aplicación nativa.
Esta actualización es muy útil para quienes trabajan con ordenadores compartidos o equipos corporativos que no permiten instalar aplicaciones. No obstante, los más beneficiados serán quienes utilicen Linux, ya que Meta nunca ha lanzado una app de escritorio oficial para WhatsApp. Las llamadas de voz y videollamadas están cifradas de extremo a extremo, no tienen un límite de tiempo y son completamente gratis.
Ahora, desde el navegador tendrás acceso a las mismas herramientas que utilizas en el móvil, como la posibilidad de compartir pantalla o usar reacciones durante la llamada. También se integrará una pestaña dedicada para revisar tu historial de llamadas y contactos favoritos.
WhatsApp mejora la calidad de vídeo y añade nuevas funciones
Otra función que debuta en esta actualización es la posibilidad de transferir una llamada grupal activa entre dispositivos sin colgar. Si empiezas una conversación desde el móvil o la tablet mientras estás fuera de casa, podrás moverla a WhatsApp Web o la aplicación de escritorio cuando llegues. Esta opción también funciona en sentido inverso.
Siguiendo con las llamadas grupales, WhatsApp estrenó una sala de espera similar a la que vemos en otras aplicaciones como Microsoft Teams. Ahora, cuando creas un enlace y activas la opción "Requerir aprobación para unirse", cada participante quedará retenido en una sala de espera hasta que el organizador de la llamada le permita entrar. Esta función es perfecta para quienes gestionan juntas del trabajo o reuniones con muchos integrantes.
Por último, Meta realizó ajustes en la calidad de video y sonido. En el caso de las videollamadas se añade QuickHD, una función que permite disfrutar el vídeo en alta definición desde los primeros segundos de la llamada. Ahora ya no tendrás que mirar imágenes pixeladas o en resolución de película pirata cuando recién empiezas a hablar, algo que es habitual en la aplicación mientras se ajusta la conexión.
En la parte del audio, WhatsApp añadió la supresión de ruido de fondo para que tu voz se escuche con claridad aunque estés en un entorno ruidoso o concurrido. Esta función es opcional y la puedes activar o desactivar en cualquier momento desde los ajustes durante una llamada.
Todas las novedades de WhatsApp Web se estarán desplegando de forma gradual y llegarán a todos los usuarios en las próximas semanas. Si todavía no puedes hacer las videollamadas desde tu navegador, no te desesperes, que pronto se activarán.

articles.title: eBay reaches $56M settlement with e-commerce newsletter writers it terrorized in 2019 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
One of the most bizarre episodes in e-commerce history has come to a close. eBay and several former eBay employees have agreed to pay $56 million to a newsletter-writing couple who were targeted by the company’s former executives in a horrific targeted harassment campaign that took place in 2019.
Ina and David Steiner, a married couple and the co-authors of EcommerceBytes, inspired the ire of high-level eBay executives after occasionally criticizing the company in their newsletter. In 2019, a plot was concocted to intimidate the couple into halting their negative coverage.
Executives used sock puppet social media accounts to harass the couple, while also sending them anonymous threatening letters and bizarre items in the mail — including live spiders and cockroaches, pornographic magazines, a bloody pig mask, a funereal wreath, and a book about surviving the death of a spouse.
According to previously released court documents, a plan that was attempted but never successfully carried out involved affixing a GPS tracking device to the couple’s car. Yet another internally broached plan involved sending a “Samoan gang” to the Steiners’ home.
The settlement this week resolves a 2021 civil case brought by the couple against eBay. The law office representing the Steiners writes that the settlement includes $46.15 million paid to the couple by eBay itself, as well as $2 million from former eBay executive CEO Devin Wenig.
Additionally, $500,000 will be paid out to the couple from former eBay executive Wendy Jones, as well as $50,000 from former eBay executive Steve Wymer. Additional funds are being paid to various non-profits.
In 2022, seven former eBay employees were criminally charged and pled guilty in relation to the plot, including the company’s former security chief, James Baugh — who was sentenced to nearly five years in prison. Others indicted by the U.S. Department of Justice include David Harville, Brian Gilbert, Stephanie Popp, Stephanie Stockwell, Philip Cooke, and former eBay contractor Veronica Zea.
In a statement published Tuesday, eBay disavowed its former employees’ behavior as “not representative of eBay’s culture” — which is comforting, I guess.
“As we have long stated, what the Steiners were subjected to by former eBay employees in 2019 was wrong, reprehensible and should never have happened,” eBay continued. “We condemn, in the strongest terms possible, the employees who perpetrated and pled guilty to criminal charges for the misconduct against Ina and David Steiner.”
“We continue to extend our deepest apologies to the Steiners. This agreement is consistent with our commitment to fairly compensate the Steiners and fulfills our efforts to make things right.”
“This case was always about more than obtaining financial recovery,” said Christopher Murphy, one of the Steiners’ attorneys. “From the beginning, our clients wanted to uncover the truth, protect journalists and publishers, hold those responsible accountable, deter future corporate misconduct, and help ensure others would never have to endure what they experienced.”

articles.title: GitHub Introduces Default "Cooldown" Policy for Dependabot Version Updates
articles.text:
Instead of immediately opening pull requests when newer dependency versions are released, Dependabot now waits three days before suggesting upgrades, thus increasing the likelihood that malicious releases are identified and removed before they can be integrated.
GitHub product manager Carlin Cherry explains the new cooldown policy by pointing to a real dependency-poisoning incident from a few years ago, when several widely used packages, collectively downloaded more than 2 billion times a week, were replaced with compromised versions. Although these versions were quickly detected and removed from npm, the roughly two hours they remained available were "more than enough time for an automated update tool to see the new version, open a pull request, and put it in front of your team".
According to Cherry,
That pattern sits behind a growing share of supply chain attacks. The malicious code rides in on a brand-new release, is published to a public registry, and gets pulled into build pipelines within minutes, before a human or a scanner has even looked at it.
To help prevent these scenarios, Dependabot now waits at least three days before opening a pull request for a dependency update after a new non-security release is published. This behavior is configurable through the cooldown option in dependabot.yml, allowing teams to tailor it to their needs. The cooldown does not apply to security updates, ensuring that fixes for publicly known vulnerabilities are not delayed.
Cherry notes that a three-day delay is emerging as a community consensus, "so this default behavior keeps Dependabot consistent as developers move between tools". The cooldown, however, does not replace the rest of defenses against other kinds of supply chain attacks:
Because a cooldown only addresses the fast-moving case, it should be one layer among several. Some additional steps to take include pinning dependencies with lockfiles, disabling install scripts in CI where you can, scoping the tokens in your build pipelines, and reviewing updates before they merge.
Reddit user broaddiscovery_941 reinforced the idea that a three day cooldown is effective:
Three days feels about right for catching the worst breakage before it hits your CI. Most dodgy releases get flagged on GitHub or Reddit within a day or two anyway, so the wait gives you time to see the drama unfold before merging anything.
On Hacker News, commenter zihotki questioned whether cooldowns could eventually become less effective, noting that "if everyone will be delaying updates", there may be "less chances to catch it in time". In response, user woodruffw argued that that the security model behind cooldowns does not rely on end users encountering malicious packages, but on dedicated security scanning efforts: "the security assumption behind cooldowns rests on security scanning parties, not on innocent users being victimized". While acknowledging that three days is a relatively short delay, they added that it should still provide sufficient lead time for these scanning systems to identify and flag threats.

articles.title: ASRock officially announces Radeon RX 9050 with 8GB VRAM — RDNA 4 card offers boost clock of up to 2600MHz (updated)
articles.text:
ASRock officially announces Radeon RX 9050 with 8GB VRAM — RDNA 4 card offers boost clock of up to 2600MHz (updated)
It would be the first and only current-gen 4GB GPU.
Update - 7/28 10:30 am ET: After taking down an earlier announcement, ASRock has officially announced the RX 9050 Challenger 8GB. As expected, the card features 8GB of GDDR6 VRAM on a 128-bit memory bus, 16 compute units, and boost clocks of up to 2600MHz. The 4GB card remains unannounced, indicating it may be exclusive to OEMs and not available for consumer purchase.
A few months ago, reports of AMD working on a new entry-level GPU began making the rounds, and today we've just got our clearest look yet at the rumored cards. ASRock has just listed the rumored Radeon RX 9050 on its website in two different configurations, 4GB and 8GB, but we have no word on pricing or availability. AMD hasn't made any official announcements yet, so we only have a limited amount of info to dissect, and it should naturally be taken with a grain of salt. However, the leaked specs from an official vendor, which have since been taken down, would herald the return of 4GB VRAM GPUs in 2026, not seen since 2022.
The RX 9050 seems to be using a cut-down Navi 44 GPU from the RX 9060 series, with 1,024 cores spread across 16 Compute Units. The leak from May claimed it had 32 CUs instead. ASRock's Challenger variant lists a 1,920 MHz base clock and a 2,600 MHz boost clock. The listing also recommends a 450W power supply, which is 50W less than the RX 9060's 500W recommendation, though we don't know the board power for the RX 9050 yet.
| SKU | GPU | Cores | Memory (GDDR6) | Memory Bus | Bandwidth | Board Power | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AMD Radeon | Navi 44 | 2,048 | 8 GB | 128-bit | 320 GB/s | 150W | 
| Intel Arc | BMG-G21 | 2,560 | 12 GB | 192-bit | 456 GB/s | 190W | 
| NVIDIA GeForce | GB206 | 3,840 | 8 GB (GDDR7) | 128-bit | 448 GB/s | 145W | 
| AMD Radeon | Navi 44 | 1,792 | 8 GB | 128-bit | 288 GB/s | 132W | 
| NVIDIA GeForce | GB207 | 2,560 | 8 GB | 128-bit | 320 GB/s | 130W | 
| AMD Radeon | Navi 44 | 1,024 | 8 GB | 128-bit | 288 GB/s | ? | 
| AMD Radeon | Navi 44 | 1,024 | 4 GB | 64-bit | 144 GB/s | ? | 
| Intel Arc | ACM-G11 | 768 | 4 GB | 64-bit | 124 GB/s | 30W | 
| NVIDIA GeForce | TU117 | 512 | 4 GB | 64-bit | 96 GB/s | 75W | 
Those were the mutual specs between both variants — the only difference lies in the memory config. The 4GB variant listing notes 4GB of GDDR6 VRAM operating over a 64-bit bus, giving us a bandwidth of 144 GB/s. We haven't seen a 4GB memory pool in GPUs since 2022, when Intel's Arc A310 and Nvidia's GTX 1630 came out. All current-gen cards have adopted 8GB as a baseline, which already gets criticized for not being future-proof.
The 8GB variant specs listed would double the bandwidth to 288 GB/s thanks to its 128-bit-wide bus. There's a chance AMD is planning to sell the 8GB to consumers directly while keeping the 4GB variant limited to OEMs. We can't say for sure since ASRock is listing it as a Challenger card on its website, but things could always change. We did find the 4GB RX 9050 already included in a CyberPower prebuilt on Best Buy, though, currently listed for $900.
The design in the leaked images appears rather generic: a black shroud with silver accents and some RGB lighting. They show two DisplayPort 2.1a and one HDMI 2.1b ports, and the card is powered via a single 8-pin PCIe connector. In terms of performance, the 8GB model should cruise through 1080p gaming, especially with the help of FSR 4. Since this is an RDNA 4 GPU, you get the full benefits of the architecture, including better ray tracing and upscaling tech.
As mentioned earlier, the last GPUs to ship with 4GB of VRAM were released four years ago. The industry is going through a turbulent period given the ongoing component crisis and memory shortage, but this would be another level of desperation.
